data: ExoMars precursor; lessons fed Rosalind Franklin
Skeleton entry for /fleet (PRD-012 v0.2 / Phase A scaffold). Builder + agency + first-flight per public sources. Specs and gallery TBD in later phases.

ESA’s 2016 ExoMars demonstrator that crashed during landing — the IMU saturated during parachute descent, causing the flight computer to believe it was below ground level; it released the parachute and fired the retrorockets for only 3 seconds instead of 30, then went silent and impacted at ~300 km/h from 3.7 km altitude. Lessons fed directly into the Rosalind Franklin lander design.
ESA's first own Mars lander attempt; intended to demonstrate EDL ahead of ExoMars Rosalind Franklin
Successor to Proton-K; modernised heavy lift
First soft landing on lunar far side
Lander of India's Chandrayaan-2; it crashed in 2019, but the orbiter kept working

ExoMars 2016 Entry, Descent, Landing Demonstrator. A control software fault caused the inertial measurement unit to saturate, leading the lander to compute a negative altitude and triggering premature parachute and backshell jettison. The thrusters fired briefly as if already on the ground, then shut off. It free-fell ~3.7 km to the surface. The flight data informed the ExoMars 2028 EDL redesign.
